newsitem.title: FRANCE: Aerospace firms agree European grouping.
newsitem.headline: Aerospace firms agree European grouping.

text.p: France's Aerospatiale, British Aerospace Plc (BAe), Daimler-Benz Aerospace (Dasa) of Germany and Spain's Casa have agreed to create a European company to manage in common all their space, defence and civil aircraft interests, Aerospatiale chairman Yves Michot said on Friday.

The firms, which are also partners in the Airbus Industrie consortium, agreed after meeting on May 26 and 27 that this the best response to the threat posed by U.S. mega-mergers such as Boeing and McDonnell Douglas, and Lockheed Martin, Michot told journalists at a seminar in southern France.
"We can't settle for (restructuring) civil aeronautics, we have to go further than that, we have to talk about all our activities," he said.

"The scheme allows companies with their programmes to come together, to have complete responsibility for programmes, use the resources of national companies, and allow them to continue to control their own assets," he said.

Current talks to change Airbus into a limited liability company would be the first step in the process of setting up what would effectively be a European holding company for civil and military aerospace.

The European grouping will comprise the four national companies, as there is no law which recognises a transnational company, and acknowledges the political reality of sovereign governments, Michot said.
He sees the eventual management system as one which takes into account the "matrix of interests between products and nationality," and makes the best use of existing resources.

The partners realised that their efforts to restructure Airbus into a limited liability company were inadequate to the scale of the U.S. threat, as that project only tackled the civilian sector, whereas the threat from America was not only one of scale but across the full range of competition in space, civil and military products.
Michot said the approach would be global, taking existing assets and finding a way to bring them under an overall management system, rather than tackling integration on a product-by-product basis.
He gave no financial or operational details of the plan but did cite Royal Dutch Shell as a bi-national company which already existed.
Defence electronics could be part of the product matrix. "Yes, why not," Michot said, when asked if electronics could be part of the European grouping.
Michot said the plan incorporated the outline of European consolidation recently presented by BAe's group managing director John Weston.

Weston told a Paris conference that he envisaged a European holding company composed initally of four national company shareholders, managing their pooled assets, maintaining centres of excellence and acting as links to national governments.

The agreement marks a breakthrough for the four firms which have up to now concentrated on efforts to restructure Airbus into a more competitive company in the face of the threat from Boeing-McDonnell Douglas.
